initialReport.text:
# N5 pointing/questions — initial independent review

## Snapshot

- Issue: https://github.com/stop-cran/learning-japanese/issues/13 — installment 2.
- Baseline: `c80d4533e613b8010b4d6e8b09f16eceeeea756c`, plus the uncommitted pointing/questions addition frozen for this review.
- Reviewed content root: `<session-files>\n5-pointing-initial-content`.
- Snapshot record: `n5-pointing-initial-review-snapshot.json`, alongside that directory.
- Review date: 2026-10-22.

I independently recalculated the following SHA-256 values over UTF-8 bytes with CRLF normalized to LF, including a final check after the review:

| Frozen file | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `articles\pointing-and-asking-questions.md` | `ad03253a8118706793660380f55d42fdeba9e8a63d08579bc19e26518fc2eb3c` |
| `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json` | `4e838945bbdeefc74317b47b4e95db25f244ce360ca524b9538c817c4dfe9226` |
| `docs\grammar-n5-pointing-sources.json` | `c6d8459837d09ab8c0e531e041f2584300e587f1494f6a3e3682b3f9d18787c4` |
| `vocabulary-records.json` | `59c700691e989e6f9811444fef03e3009f5b6408edae1a05924dd133d765b85e` |

All file:line references below refer to these frozen versions, using repository-relative paths for the three repository files.

## Scope

**Reviewer:** one GitHub Copilot reviewer in this session; no delegation or second reviewer. **Actual runtime model ID: unavailable** in the exposed runtime information; no model ID is inferred from the parent, author metadata, or product name.

Read and assessed:

- The complete 212-line article, including every example, translation, table, qualification and link.
- All **54 complete exercise objects**: all prompts, question-side instructions/translations, evidence, explanations, targets, levels, accepted forms, options, option rationales, additional correct options and vocabulary payloads.
- All **194 accepted renderings, 162 base options, ten additional correct options, 81 lexical spans and 219 exclusions**. Exercise objects were read in complete-object batches, not sampled.
- All 27 construction definitions, ten relationships, ten introduction groups, 27 facets, 54 membership records, four soft recommendations and the absence of hard prerequisites.
- The complete neutral source/coverage record, all 19 assigned primary anchors and the secondary どうやって mapping.
- The supplied installment work item; `.github\copilot-instructions.md`; the applicable grammar, answer-set, introduction-group and vocabulary contracts in `docs\content-format.md`; `docs\grammar-authoring-sources.md`; and `REVIEW.md`'s reusable grammar-review lessons.
- The actual meaning sections of the 16 linked word cards, and the relevant linked sections of the basic-particle, topic/inclusion, adjective-foundation and restriction/inclusion articles. This was a link/sense-fit check, not a complete re-review of those unchanged articles.

Repository access was read-only. No content, instruction, inventory, manifest or repository file was edited. The only authored file is this report. No commit, push, issue update, delegation, build or importer run was performed.

**Independence disclosure:** while locating the required reusable lessons, my initial `REVIEW.md` range also returned historical review/author summaries for unrelated earlier batches, including foundations. I then narrowed the reading to the reusable-lessons section. Thus this pass was not perfectly blind to unrelated historical summaries. No earlier pointing/questions reviewer report or pointing/questions author verdict was consulted, and prior-batch conclusions were not used as evidence for this installment.

## Verdicts

| Reviewed deliverable | Correctness | Scoped coverage | Comprehensibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete pointing/questions article | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** |
| Complete exercise set and associated metadata | **CLEAN** | **NEEDS FIX** | **NEEDS FIX** |

For this table, correctness concerns the Japanese constructions, completed accepted/model sentences, translations and substantive grammatical contrasts; the answer-set omissions are recorded under scoped coverage/fairness. **No incorrect Japanese model answer or required grammatical distinction was established.** Exercise coverage needs the bounded typed-answer fixes in F02/F03, and comprehensibility needs the inconsistent statement feedback fixed in F01. In particular, F01 is not classified as a failure of Japanese grammatical correctness.

**CLEAN** means no actionable defect established in the indicated facet of this bounded scope. It is not native-speaker certification, exhaustive language coverage, or evidence of mastery.

### Coverage and interaction assessment

| Assigned material | Coverage actually inspected |
| --- | --- |
| これ／それ／あれ／どれ — primary IDs **5, 11, 19, 712** | Physical-perspective table, change of speaker, stated scene boundaries; eight thing-context tasks. |
| この／その／あの／どの — **30, 37, 47, 713** | Noun retention, no extra の, intervening adjective, selection; eight modifier-context tasks and four shared phrase-formation tasks. |
| ここ／そこ／あそこ／どこ — **14, 20, 29, 56** | Physical places, shared-space qualification, existence versus activity case roles; eight place-context tasks. |
| Question か — **8** | Polite predicate completion, no inversion, plain-noun caution; four ending tasks and the whole-question interpretation material. |
| 誰 — **714** | Subject versus approached-person roles; two person questions with retained が／に. |
| なぜ／どうして／なんで — **1094, 1095, 1096** | Qualified register tendencies and overlapping reason answers; two shared-answer reason tasks, not three artificially exclusive meanings. |
| 何か／何も — **718** | Unspecified versus negative-none constructions, optional object/subject marking, negative-question warning; four formation tasks plus interpretation support. |
| 誰か／どこか／誰も／どこも — **721** | Retained に／と／へ and particle order, whole negative scope; eight person/place formation tasks and relevant interpretation tasks. |
| どうやって — secondary source | Method/means explanation and two method tasks; method is also a substantive fixed-option alternative throughout the six information tasks. |

The primary index's actual embedded data independently confirmed every assigned ID/title/level mapping. Its ID **369**, そんな・こんな・あんな・どんな, is **JLPT4**. The article correctly leaves that family optional; it is not required by an N5 exercise here. Index labels were used for curriculum placement, not as linguistic proof. Neither lexical-card levels nor kanji difficulty determined these verdicts.

The advertised split of **30 context selections, 20 formation tasks and four interpretations** fits the actual tasks. These are scaffolded exercises, as the article says. The scene exercises give the speaker/listener relationship or an explicit distant-from-both framing; an invisible picture is not required. The four phrase tasks explicitly require replacement or noun retention, so their otherwise grammatical alternative phrases are fair distractors under that visible operation.

The four interpretation instructions give readings and operational meanings for **both** 不特定 and 全否定, in identical answer-independent order. They do not systematically put the correct definition first. The metalinguistic labels are supported response labels, not unannounced vocabulary prerequisites.

The negative and indefinite tasks retain the relevant case roles and polarity. A negative ending is not treated as an automatic instruction to use も. In particular, the forgotten-item question and arrival question do not assert a positive answer. The article's warning against treating all も as “nothing/nobody” is adequate within its stated boundaries.

### Metadata and vocabulary assessment

- Every exercise has one authored introduction-group owner. Each of the 27 facets targets one construction and has two distinct example keys.
- The 25 distinct key strings are conservative group/context metadata, not 25 independently sampled discourse situations. Paired positive/negative and phrase-retention/replacement examples appropriately share keys. No actionable grouping defect was established.
- All four recommendation targets exist, remain soft, and have reasons fitting the connected material. There are no hard prerequisites.
- Every relationship construction is targeted; all coverage-record exercise references exist; every exercise has one complete-task level-decision mapping.
- All 54 prompt hashes, inventory context hashes and vocabulary-payload hashes matched the frozen objects. The 81 spans plus 219 exclusions cover the prompts exactly once, with matching offsets/text and no gaps or overlap.
- Readings match the displayed stems and words. Case particles, endings, tested expressions and interpretation blanks are protected instead of supplied as answer hints. Local-only glosses make no canonical word-card claim.
- The article's あの link goes to the hesitation card **only in the explicit hesitation warning**, not as purported evidence for the demonstrative. The other linked word senses and the inspected cross-article destinations fit their stated purposes.
- The model option is accepted in every object; no base distractor collides with an accepted answer after trim/NFKC normalization; every additional correct label belongs to the corresponding accepted set. These mechanical checks support, but do not replace, the full linguistic reading.

## Findings

### N5PQ-F01 — statement tasks describe a “requested question” in their feedback

- **Severity:** Minor.
- **Facet:** Comprehensibility / local feedback consistency.
- **File:lines:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:1820–1827,1868–1875`.
- **Objects:** `n5-pointing-ending-quiet-statement`; `n5-pointing-ending-museum-statement`.
- **Claim:** Both tasks explicitly request a statement and correctly accept です or ます, but their explanations say that adding か “makes the requested question.” No question was requested. The shared question-side suffix “with か for a question” can be understood conditionally, but the explanation's definite “requested question” directly contradicts these objects.
- **Impact:** A learner who correctly completes 部屋は静かです or 博物館は毎朝九時に開きます receives feedback apparently directing them toward the rejected question answer. This is a localized interaction defect, not evidence that either completed Japanese statement is wrong.
- **Remedy:** Make these two explanations local: です／ます completes the requested statement; adding か would instead ask a question. If retaining one shared instruction template, phrase the condition explicitly: add か **only when a question is requested**. Preserve the keys and accepted answers.
- **Evidence:** The quoted translation, accepted list and explanation conflict within each complete object. [Tofugu, “か for Asking Questions”](https://www.tofugu.com/japanese-grammar/particle-ka/) confirms the statement/question operation; its casual-question qualifications do not alter these expressly polite formation tasks.
- **Confidence:** High.

### N5PQ-F02 — four typed-answer classes omit the recognized spelling of an already accepted expression

- **Severity:** Minor.
- **Facet:** Scoped coverage / typed-answer fairness.
- **File:lines:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:1935–1941,1982–1988,2169–2179,2240–2250`.
- **Objects and omissions:**

| Object | Already accepted | Missing spelling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n5-pointing-information-interpreter` | どなた | **何方**（どなた） |
| `n5-pointing-information-ask-source` | どなた | **何方**（どなた） |
| `n5-pointing-information-transport` | どう | **如何**（どう） |
| `n5-pointing-information-cutting` | どう | **如何**（どう） |

- **Claim:** These are spellings of expressions the tasks already accept and explain, not requests to introduce a new synonym, grammatical sense or harder contrast. No visible kana-only restriction is present. NFKC does not turn either spelling into its accepted kana equivalent.
- **Impact:** A fitting typed completion such as 何方が通訳しますか or 病院まで如何行きますか is outside the authored acceptance list solely because of spelling. The main kana model should remain preferred; rarity does not make the same recognized expression an incorrect grammar answer under this repository's stated spelling policy.
- **Remedy:** Add 何方 to the two person-question lists and 如何 to the two method lists. Retain existing kana models, explanations and construction identities. Do not create separate semantic buttons, raise required levels, or imply equal spelling frequency.
- **Evidence:** Independently inspected JMdict entries through Jisho's API: [どなた](https://jisho.org/api/v1/search/words?keyword=%E3%81%A9%E3%81%AA%E3%81%9F), entry `何方-1`, gives written 何方, reading どなた, sense “who,” with respectful-language and usually-kana tags; [どう](https://jisho.org/api/v1/search/words?keyword=%E3%81%A9%E3%81%86), the **如何** entry rather than the unrelated 銅／胴 entries, gives reading どう and “how; in what way; how about,” usually in kana. The supplied exercise explanations already license the relevant person/method readings. The repository contract explicitly distinguishes spelling recognition from normalization.
- **Confidence:** High. This is dictionary-backed recognition, not a frequency claim.

### N5PQ-F03 — person-indefinite formation silently excludes the fitting polite person variant

- **Severity:** Minor.
- **Facet:** Scoped coverage / typed-answer fairness and visible formation boundaries.
- **File:lines:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:2502–2510,2543–2551,2584–2592,2625–2633`.
- **Objects:** `n5-pointing-indef-people-some-ask`; `n5-pointing-indef-people-none-ask`; `n5-pointing-indef-people-some-talk`; `n5-pointing-indef-people-none-talk`.
- **Claim:** The visible task requires an indefinite/negative person phrase and a retained に or と, but does not require the base 誰 or exclude respectful どなた. The following fitting completions are absent:
  - どなたかに聞きます — ask someone;
  - どなたにも聞きません — ask no one;
  - どなたかと話します — talk with someone;
  - どなたとも話しません — talk with no one.
  These preserve the exact か-before-case / case-before-も operation and the supplied polarity. The setting supplies no incompatible casual-only register. The set itself recognizes どなた as an accepted person alternative in the two information questions.
- **Impact:** Typed mode can reject a natural, more respectful realization of the requested construction for a restriction disclosed only by the answer list. Fixed-option mode remains usable; the two authored choices do not become ambiguous.
- **Remedy:** Prefer accepting the corresponding どなた forms, with a short respectful-register explanation and their recognized 何方 spellings. Alternatively, if practising formation specifically from **誰** is the actual intended learning operation, name that base explicitly in the pre-answer instruction, as the thing tasks already name their 何か／何も family. Do not present the omitted polite construction as ungrammatical.
- **Evidence:** [Bunpro 誰, actual main “Caution”](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/だれ), independently read from the main HTML rather than forum extraction, identifies どなた as the respectful person expression. [Bunpro's actual indefinite Structure/About](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/誰か-どこか-誰も-どこも) establishes the retained-case ordering; the JMdict 何方（どなた）entry establishes lexical identity. Independently inspected [どなたか sentence results](https://jisho.org/search/どなたか%20%23sentences) include Jreibun `7067/1`, an unspecified-person request; [どなたにも results](https://jisho.org/search/どなたにも%20%23sentences) include Tatoeba `122139`, 日曜日はどなたにもお会いしません, demonstrating negative-none rather than an affirmative-everyone reading. The four completions above are applications to the reviewed prompts, not claims that those exact sentences were corpus quotations.
- **Confidence:** High that the completions preserve the requested person/case/polarity meanings; medium-high that omission is actionable under these broadly worded formation instructions. Naming a genuine base-word restriction would resolve the acceptance-boundary issue without expanding the required syllabus.

## Optional

### N5PQ-O01 — polish the templated pointing feedback

- **Facet:** Comprehensibility; nonblocking editorial polish.
- **File:lines:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:243,527,983,985,1439` and equivalent repeated rationales.
- “the an unknown identity or location” is a repeated English template error. In the book-selection instruction, “the unknown owner's selection” is also less precise than “which book belongs to the listener”: the person is known; the book is being identified.
- **Suggested treatment:** Remove the doubled article and describe the actual missing identity/location. The existing English question and Japanese prompt already make the keyed task understandable, so these are not additional correctness failures.
- **Evidence/confidence:** Direct text; high.

### N5PQ-O02 — make the generic feedback more sentence-specific

- **Facet:** Comprehensibility; nonblocking feedback improvement.
- **File:lines:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:1942–1957,1989–2004,2933–2936`.
- The person-question alternatives are explained only as “Requests the reason” / “Requests the method or means.” In the literal blanks, なぜが通訳しますか and どうやってに聞きましたか also fail because the printed が／に needs the appropriate person phrase; they are not merely alternative well-formed information questions. The main explanation's retained-role instruction keeps the task interpretable, but the distractor feedback could explicitly connect to it.
- The arrival interpretation's final explanatory sentence instead discusses the forgotten-item question. That is a valid cross-example observation, but a local sentence explaining the two か in 誰か来ましたか would be clearer.
- **Suggested treatment:** Explain the actual completed distractor where relevant and localize the arrival feedback, without changing answer sets or declaring shared reason/method readings mutually exclusive.
- **Evidence/confidence:** Complete prompts, options and explanations; high.

## Sources independently checked

These checks support the verdicts and boundaries; they do not imply that a site's every claim was adopted.

- **Tofugu:** main Basics/Patterns of Use and relevant perspective/discourse sections for [これ・それ・あれ・どれ](https://www.tofugu.com/japanese-grammar/kore-sore-are-dore/), [この・その・あの・どの](https://www.tofugu.com/japanese-grammar/kono-sono-ano-dono/) and [ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ](https://www.tofugu.com/japanese-grammar/koko-soko-asoko-doko/); the [か](https://www.tofugu.com/japanese-grammar/particle-ka/) polite-question, indefinite-pronoun and intonation sections. The article appropriately qualifies physical distance and avoids turning the usual three-or-more teaching convention into an unrestricted conversational ban.
- **Bunpro:** actual main Structure/About sections for 何か／何も and 誰か／どこか／誰も／どこも, actual main 誰 section, and the main [なぜ](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/なぜ), [どうして](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/どうして) and [なんで](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/なんで) explanations. The なんで Caution explicitly distinguishes the clearer means reading なにで. The initial simplified 何か／何も extraction was a forum reply; it was not treated as the main lesson or used to ban を.
- **JMdict through Jisho:** exact relevant entries and readings for all 12 pointing expressions, plus どうして, どなた, どう and 何か. Homophones, other readings and interjections were distinguished from the required sense. The entry 如何して supports both method and reason senses; that is not a claim of equal naturalness in every context. The supplied method scenes make their intended information explicit.
- **JLPT Sensei:** actual main HTML for [どうやって](https://jlptsensei.com/learn-japanese-grammar/%e3%81%a9%e3%81%86%e3%82%84%e3%81%a3%e3%81%a6-douyatte-meaning/), including the explicit **Level: JLPT N5**, meaning/use and eight visible examples. Its embedded-question example was not imported into this set's required grammar.
- **Tae Kim:** intact HTML of [“Using question words” and “Question words with inclusive meaning”](https://guidetojapanese.org/learn/grammar/question), including 誰かが, どれかを, 誰か知りませんか and どこにも行かなかった. The simplified extraction omitted Japanese, so it was not sufficient evidence by itself.
- **Jisho sentence results:** actual indefinite [何かを](https://jisho.org/search/何かを%20%23sentences) examples, including Jreibun `1608/2` and `3777/3`, support retained object marking. Embedded-question matches on the same result page were not confused with indefinite “something.” The polite-person examples are identified under F03.

## Limits

- This is an **initial** report tied to the four frozen hashes. No later diff, correction or reconciliation has been reviewed here.
- The independence limitation concerning the initial `REVIEW.md` range is disclosed in Scope. No model comparison or claim of a perfectly blinded historical context is made.
- A dictionary API request for 何も encountered HTTP 429; its negative “not anything/nothing” sense was subsequently inspected on the normal entry page. Simplified Bunpro, Tae Kim and JLPT Sensei extraction gaps were addressed through their actual HTML. No consequential linguistic conclusion remains unresolved because of those retrieval problems.
- Dictionary recognition supports accepted orthography, not everyday frequency. The review does not require teaching rare spellings as preferred models, accepting every archaic reading, or extending these tasks to an unbounded set of paraphrases.
- The article's explicitly deferred discourse pointing, full affirmative question-word patterns, embedded questions, casual-question system and optional N4 どんな family were not demanded as independently scored facets.
- No full re-review of unchanged linked articles/cards, Android UI execution, importer validation, native-speaker certification, corpus-wide frequency study, or measured learning outcome is claimed. The inline read-only checks were limited to the frozen package and its review inventory.
- Three minor actionable findings remain for adjudication/reconciliation. The two optional items are nonblocking. No major or critical defect was established.

Add 何方 to both existing どなた answer classes and 如何 to both existing どう classes: four spelling renderings, no new buttons or grammar distinctions.
Accept the four respectful どなた case/polarity forms and their 何方 spellings: eight renderings. Explain respectful register without artificially narrowing the visible tasks.
Remove the repeated doubled article from all affected pointing explanations/rationales; identify the unknown book rather than an unknown owner.
Tie person-question distractors to their printed case marker and give the arrival and forgotten-item questions local feedback. Do not assert that every possible なぜに phrase is ungrammatical.

# N5 pointing/questions — same-reviewer reconciliation

## Snapshot

- Issue: https://github.com/stop-cran/learning-japanese/issues/13 — installment 2.
- Baseline: `c80d4533e613b8010b4d6e8b09f16eceeeea756c`, plus the revised uncommitted pointing/questions addition.

- Initial report: `n5-pointing-initial-independent-review.md`.
- Initial frozen content: `n5-pointing-initial-content`.
- Revised snapshot record: `n5-pointing-revised-review-snapshot.json`.
- Session artifacts are under `<session-files>`.

The following normalized-LF SHA-256 values were independently verified:

| Reviewed input | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `articles\pointing-and-asking-questions.md` | `c9797398bff7d5f6ee5f0aec1137dc2ee28e936f969c2f5bd6dededff0259610` |
| `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json` | `66b9d5ef401f436823d1dc77cba41a1e51c789e30b31d3b2f6e30df042062364` |
| `n5-pointing-reconciliation.diff` | `b3ff0b13238259279308c863211c53deb21c80b1f58d46a8c312db2c37f45230` |
| `n5-pointing-reconciliation-packet.json` | `889d01e92901f06057b0a6a5d060eeb37818cba0bfe70e86f54138e2e1efabca` |

The supplied diff exactly matches a fresh in-memory unified diff between the frozen initial article/exercise file and the two current runtime files. All 38 packet objects match their current-file objects and their inclusive line ranges.

The initial report is preserved, including its initial verdicts and limitations. Its **raw-byte** SHA-256 remains `fe8317371d744f7d2951c65a781ba2d9748d1b81fc7dead4b947d297af8f21b7`; this raw-byte value is deliberately distinguished from the normalized-LF hashes above.

Unless otherwise stated, file:line references below identify the revised runtime files at the hashes above.

## Scope

**Reviewer:** the same GitHub Copilot reviewer who performed the initial pass, now conducting an informed reconciliation against that report, the actual diff and the supplied adjudication. **Actual runtime model ID: unavailable.** No model is inferred from author metadata or the parent. No delegation or second reviewer was used.

Read and assessed in this pass:

- The entire 498-line runtime diff.
- All revised article passages with surrounding context: the respectful-person addition, retained-case extension, register qualification and source link. The revised article has 216 lines.
- All **38 complete changed exercise objects**, including their unchanged fields, completed accepted forms, base/additional choices, rationales, translations, instructions, explanations and vocabulary payloads.
- All **38 complete updated vocabulary inventory records**, including their exclusions and revision-bound hashes.
- All packet adjudications, changed-field lists, added-answer lists, exact ranges and unchanged IDs.

The changed-object subset contains **126 accepted renderings, 128 base options, four additional correct options, 57 lexical spans and 153 exclusions**. These are the full contents of the changed objects, not just the added strings.

The **composite reviewed set** remains 54 tasks, now with **206 accepted renderings, 162 base options, ten additional correct options, 81 lexical spans and 219 exclusions**. The 27 constructions, ten relationships, ten groups, 27 facets, four soft recommendations and absence of hard prerequisites are preserved.

### Explicit carry-forward

This is **not a second complete initial audit**. The initial review is carried forward for the unchanged article teaching, previously inspected source/level coverage and link targets, unchanged construction/relationship/group metadata, and the following **16 unchanged complete exercise objects**:

```text
n5-pointing-indef-places-none-key
n5-pointing-indef-places-none-trip
n5-pointing-indef-places-some-key
n5-pointing-indef-places-some-trip
n5-pointing-indef-things-none-box
n5-pointing-indef-things-none-shopping
n5-pointing-indef-things-some-box
n5-pointing-indef-things-some-shopping
n5-pointing-information-absence
n5-pointing-information-study
n5-pointing-phrase-noun-book-request
n5-pointing-phrase-noun-box-selection
n5-pointing-phrase-standalone-book-request
n5-pointing-phrase-standalone-box-selection
n5-pointing-scope-no-arrivals
n5-pointing-scope-no-trip
```

An in-memory comparison independently confirmed that this is exactly the unchanged-object set. No exercise was omitted from the initial-plus-reconciliation scope.

**Preserved independence disclosure:** while locating the required reusable lessons during the initial pass, my first `REVIEW.md` range also returned unrelated historical review/author summaries, including foundations. The initial pass was therefore not perfectly blind to unrelated historical summaries. No earlier pointing/questions reviewer report or pointing/questions author verdict was consulted in that initial pass. This reconciliation intentionally uses my own initial report and the requested adjudication; it does not manufacture a new claim of perfect blinding.

Repository access remained read-only. This reconciliation report is the only file authored in this pass.

## Verdicts

| Composite reviewed deliverable | Correctness | Scoped coverage | Comprehensibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Article: initial review carried forward, plus revised passages checked | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** |
| Exercise set: 38 complete changed objects reconciled, 16 unchanged objects carried forward | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** |

All three actionable initial findings are **resolved**. Both adopted optional items are also **resolved**, without retroactively reclassifying them as blocking defects. No new actionable defect or consequential unresolved linguistic claim was established within this composite scope.

The initial exercise coverage/comprehensibility **NEEDS FIX** verdicts remain valid for the initial snapshot; this report supersedes them only for the revised snapshot above. The initial correctness verdict was not a claim that every feedback sentence or answer list was complete, and F01 remains a feedback-consistency issue rather than a Japanese grammatical error.

**CLEAN** means no actionable defect established within this bounded reviewed scope, not native-speaker certification, exhaustive correctness, mastery, or publication authorization.

## Findings — individual reconciliation

### N5PQ-F01 — resolved

- **Original severity/facet:** Minor; comprehensibility / local statement feedback.
- **Revised locations:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:1711–1758,1759–1814,1815–1862,1863–1926`.
- **Original claim and impact:** The two statement tasks correctly accepted です／ます but described adding か as making the “requested question,” contradicting the requested assertion.
- **Verified remedy:** Both statement explanations now say that です or ます completes the requested polite statement, and that adding か would instead ask a question the task does not request. All four related instructions explicitly say to add か **only when a question is requested**.
- **Evidence/regression check:** Read all four complete objects. 部屋は静かです and 博物館は毎朝九時に開きます remain the statement completions; 田中さんは先生ですか and 明日、駅に行きますか remain the question completions. Keys, alternatives and visible ordinary-affirmative-nonpast restrictions agree. The question-task explanations remain appropriate to their own contexts.
- **Remaining impact/remedy:** None; no further change needed for this finding.
- **Confidence:** High.

### N5PQ-F02 — resolved

- **Original severity/facet:** Minor; scoped coverage / typed spelling acceptance.
- **Revised locations:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:1927–1974,1975–2022,2163–2234,2235–2306`.
- **Original claim and impact:** Four lists rejected recognized spellings of expressions already accepted in kana.
- **Verified remedy:** Both person-question lists now include **何方** for already accepted どなた; both method-question lists include **如何** for already accepted どう. Exactly four renderings were added for this finding.
- **Evidence/regression check:** The complete objects preserve the person and method readings established in the initial review's exact JMdict entries. I checked the literal completions: 何方が通訳しますか, 何方に聞きましたか, 病院まで如何行きますか and 段ボールを如何切りますか. Existing model choices and explanations remain intact. The additions are spelling recognition, not new grammar targets, separate correct buttons or claims of equal spelling frequency.
- **Remaining impact/remedy:** None.
- **Confidence:** High.

### N5PQ-F03 — resolved

- **Original severity/facet:** Minor; scoped coverage / fitting polite-person alternatives and visible formation boundaries.
- **Revised locations:** `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:2501–2543,2544–2586,2587–2629,2630–2672`; `articles\pointing-and-asking-questions.md:120,163–165,207–208`.
- **Original claim and impact:** Broad person-phrase instructions did not exclude respectful どなた, but the answer lists rejected its fitting retained-case forms.
- **Verified remedy:** The four respective tasks now accept:
  - **どなたかに／何方かに** before 聞きます;
  - **どなたにも／何方にも** before 聞きません;
  - **どなたかと／何方かと** before 話します;
  - **どなたとも／何方とも** before 話しません.
  These are eight added renderings. The explanations identify the respectful register and recognized spelling, keeping kana as the ordinary model.
- **Evidence/regression check:** Read the complete objects and formed every new sentence. The additions preserve the requested unspecified-person or negative-none meaning, the に／と role, and か-before-case / case-before-も order. No old answer was removed, no hidden family restriction was introduced, and the ordinary 誰 forms remain sufficient.
- **Article check:** The new wording accurately presents どなた as a more respectful person expression, applies the same case ordering, and explicitly avoids promising that one respectful word makes every surrounding expression honorific. It neither requires a new honorific-predicate contrast nor asserts unrestricted interchangeability in every social situation.
- **Source evidence:** The initial review's inspected main Bunpro 誰/indefinite sections and exact JMdict evidence remain applicable. I additionally inspected the actual newly linked [Jisho どなた page](https://jisho.org/search/どなた): it presents 何方（どなた）, “who,” with respectful-language and usually-kana tags, and 何方か（どなたか）, “someone,” with the corresponding register qualification. The link fits the added claim. Its vocabulary-level label was **not** used to assign grammar difficulty.
- **Remaining impact/remedy:** None.
- **Confidence:** High. The acceptance-based remedy removes the original instruction-boundary concern without requiring the narrower alternative remedy.

### New actionable findings

**None.** No new finding ID is needed. No initial finding is partially resolved, unresolved or withdrawn.

## Optional — adopted items reconciled

### N5PQ-O01 — resolved; originally optional polish

- **Facet/locations:** Comprehensibility; all 24 pointing objects in `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:206–1536`, especially the book-selection object at `977–1027`.
- **Verified change:** The repeated “the an” template error is removed from the affected explanations and rationales. The book-selection instruction now asks **which book belongs to the listener**, rather than describing an unknown owner.
- **Evidence/impact:** All 24 complete revised pointing objects were read. The corrected English retains the original speaker/listener/distant perspective, noun versus standalone distinction, and unknown-identity/location task. The book, not its already identified owner, is now correctly described as unknown.
- **Residual recommendation:** None; this stays an adopted nonblocking improvement, not a retrospective correctness failure.
- **Confidence:** High.

### N5PQ-O02 — resolved; originally optional feedback improvement

- **Facet/locations:** Comprehensibility; `grammar\n5-pointing-questions.json:1927–2022,2899–2980`.
- **Verified change:** Person-question distractors now explain why they fail to supply the **intended person phrase** before the printed が or に. The wording is scoped to this task; it does not assert that every possible なぜに expression is ungrammatical.
- **Interpretation check:** The arrival explanation now distinguishes the indefinite か in 誰か from final question か and correctly says the question leaves whether anyone came open. The forgotten-item explanation is local to an unspecified forgotten thing and still rejects the mistaken “nothing was forgotten” interpretation.
- **Evidence/impact:** Read all four complete objects, including unchanged instructions, choices, accepted labels and lexical hints. The 不特定／全否定 definitions and readings remain question-side and answer-independent. No assertion of actual arrival, change of polarity or answer-revealing hint was introduced.
- **Residual recommendation:** None.
- **Confidence:** High.

No new optional expansion is requested.

## Bounded regression and integrity checks

These checks were performed directly by this reviewer, in memory, against the supplied package and the two identified runtime files. They are **not** a claim to have run the parent's publication/integration checks.

- Confirmed the actual 38 changed IDs and 16 unchanged IDs against the frozen initial JSON, and confirmed every packet object's fields, added-answer list and inclusive locator.
- Confirmed preservation of every prompt, exercise order/identity, target, relationship, level, answer key, evidence field, vocabulary payload and additional-correct-option object. Base option IDs/labels are preserved; only the disclosed rationales changed.
- Confirmed every old accepted answer is retained in its existing list order, with exactly **12** appended renderings: four spelling forms and eight respectful-person forms. Total acceptance is **194 → 206**.
- Confirmed all model labels and additional correct options remain accepted, with no normalized duplicate accepted answers or accepted-string collision with a base distractor.
- Confirmed all non-exercise top-level metadata is unchanged, including construction definitions, relationships, groups, facets, member keys and recommendation/prerequisite fields.
- Recomputed the 38 updated context fingerprints and prompt/vocabulary hashes. Each record matches its complete changed object. Apart from `contextSha256`, those records are identical to the corresponding frozen initial records; exclusions, provenance and statuses were not silently altered.
- Checked the 57 lexical spans and 153 exclusions belonging to the changed objects: offsets/text still match the unchanged prompts and cover each prompt exactly once. Their local readings/glosses remain compatible with the revised context, and target expressions/polarity remain protected.
- The original **19-primary-anchor plus secondary どうやって** coverage assessment carries forward. The new respectful alternatives are optional accepted realizations, not harder required contrasts. The どんな family remains optional N4; no exercise newly requires it. The initial scaffolding and no-mastery qualifications remain appropriate.

## Limits

- This is a **same-reviewer, informed reconciliation**, not a new independent reviewer, a second full source audit, or a model comparison. The initial disclosure about incidental exposure to unrelated historical `REVIEW.md` summaries remains in force.
- Unchanged teaching, 16 unchanged exercises, source/level coverage and metadata carry forward the initial review explicitly. Existing linked articles/cards were not re-audited.
- Only the new どなた link was freshly checked on the web in this pass. Previously established linguistic evidence for the other fixes is carried forward from the initial report; no new source-retrieval claim is made for those entries.
- Dictionary-backed orthography does not establish equal usage frequency. Broader honorific usage, every possible paraphrase, and the article's expressly deferred constructions are outside this reconciliation.
- I did **not** run repository content validation, manifest regeneration, the global vocabulary gate, Android importer tests, app/UI checks or corpus-wide preservation tests. The parent separately owns those checks; their outcomes are not attributed to this reviewer. The package comparisons above are narrower.
- No repository content, instructions, inventory, manifest or prior report was edited; no commit or push was performed. The only new artifact is this reconciliation report.
- At the pinned revised snapshot, **no actionable content defect or consequential unresolved linguistic claim remains within the composite scope**. No further linguistic review loop is required merely to prolong agreement.
